children: CEO Jensen Huang tapped the brakes on the increasing rhetoric around a potential cataclysmic catastrophe posed by artificial intelligence systems.
Instead, he said AI executives are likely drumming up this rhetoric in an attempt to avoid existing laws during an interview with CBS on Sunday morning.
"2030 is not going to be the end of the world," Huang said. "There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world."
Huang was directly referring to Anthropic's

that there is a greater than 10% chance that AI will destroy all humans within the next decade. Huang indicated that current legislation covers many of the concerns, and executives calling for new national and international frameworks are attempting to avoid those.

"You have cybersecurity unauthorized entry laws; you have damage liabilities," Huang said. "If your product does harm, if your product doesn't perform as you promised, and if you entered into contracts with companies for service level agreements, there are plenty of laws associated with that. My point is, apply those first. And don't let this doomsday narrative cause somebody to relieve them of the laws that currently exist."
Huang's comments echoed Trump's statements from last week that the AI doomsday pronouncements were a "hoax." Trump doubled down on that over the weekend, announcing his intent to create a federal
"We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry," Trump posted on social media. "Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it as it grows!"
"However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System," Trump added.
